text: # Synthetic applicability and open items [AP01] C01 is a COLD-profile unit tested at 5 degrees with a current cold-fixture certificate; its limit is 150 milliseconds. N01, N02, N03, and E17 were tested at 20 degrees under NORMAL. No valid HOT qualification or authorized threshold above 30 degrees is supplied. The packet therefore does not establish a claim of qualification across every temperature. This missing scope is not a measurement proving that all hot operation physically fails. An analyst should state the unsupported extension precisely rather than discard the bounded favorable evidence for C01 or N01. [AP02] N03 lacks channel B measurement and a third valid repeated run. Its second attempted trace aborted before acquisition and has no delay value. X99 has a raw 85-millisecond number but is explicitly invalid because synchronization was lost. It cannot contribute to N03 or any other unit's valid-run count. The correct support-gap finding identifies the exact missing channel and repetition, relevant requirement, and unavailable evidence. It does not predict what the unmeasured channel would have done. Invalid, missing, and explicitly failing measurements have different meanings and must remain distinguishable in the report. [AP03] The packet provides no argument about population defect rates, lifetime reliability, network threats, mechanical strength, or an unrestricted meaning of safe. The finite release conjunction is narrower than universal design safety. Aesthetic opinions about the clarity or beauty of a specification are likewise outside the threshold predicates unless a separate criterion is supplied. The exercise is a reasoning fixture using invented documents, not guidance for deploying a real safety system. Favorable arithmetic and complete signatures can support the specified synthetic release route without supporting unbounded real-world conclusions.
